firstOccurrence.englishText: Nebuchadnezzar the king made an image of gold, whose height was sixty cubits,* A cubit is the length from the tip of the middle finger to the elbow on a man’s arm, or about 18 inches or 46 centimeters. and its width six cubits. He set it up in the plain of Dura, in the province of Babylon.

definitions.full: H1757. Dura דּוּרָא proper name, of a location near Babylonia , only ד ׳בִּקְעַת Dan 3:1 , ᵐ5 . τοῦ περιβόλου (Syro-Hex. περίβολον ), Θ Δεειρα ; Dûru is name of several places in Babylonia Dl Par. 216 ; Baer Dn. p. x , compare Andr M 58 *; Hoffm Pers. Märtyrer 164 f. ; name of small river and mounds Opp Expéd. i. 238 f. (see Dr); improbably explained as = zôr , depression (name actually used of lower Euphrase and Tigris valleys) by Wetzst De Jes:3 701f. ; Babylonian dûru = wall.
